decisions.reason: As a training offer that extends the firm's established application-support business, it is strategically complementary, low-cost to maintain, and likely to remain part of the broader service portfolio even if marketed less visibly.

A fourth rotary axis accessory fits well with the firm's precision machining customers and installed machine base, so it is likely to be retained unless replaced by a newer generation or folded into standard configurations.

Because hybrid additive post-processing is relatively distant from the firm's core milling and dispensing offer, a medium-sized machinery firm would be more likely to discontinue it if demand, fit, or service economics proved weaker than expected.
A high-speed CNC milling machine line is close to the firm's core capabilities, central to customer demand, and consistent with its R&D-led growth path, making withdrawal unlikely.

An automatic tool change system directly supports productivity and workflow efficiency in the firm's existing machinery offer, so it is likely to stay unless superseded by an upgraded integrated solution.
